Officials say the negotiations will also touch on issues such as social security coordination, tax compliance, and data protection to ensure a comprehensive and mutually beneficial partnership.

While the final terms remain under negotiation, the initiative signals Canada’s intent to deepen its engagement with the EU and to provide Canadians with greater flexibility in pursuing professional and educational opportunities abroad. The outcome of Carney’s talks will be closely watched by both governments and the business community, as it could reshape the landscape of international mobility for Canadian citizens in the coming years.
author: Euronews

title: Russia Begins Early Voting in Donetsk Ahead of Parliamentary Election
content:
Russia has begun early voting for its parliamentary elections in the Russian‑controlled areas of Ukraine’s Donetsk region, according to reports from local authorities. Election officials and voters are being escorted by armed personnel as the process commences, underscoring the heightened security measures in place.

The early voting session is part of Russia’s broader parliamentary election schedule, which is being held across territories it claims control over. In Donetsk, the presence of armed personnel is intended to ensure the orderly conduct of the vote, although observers note that the security presence is a common feature in contested regions.

The start of early voting marks a significant step in Russia’s effort to legitimize its governance in the region, while also highlighting the ongoing tensions and the complex political status of Donetsk under Russian administration.
author: Euronews

title: NATO shoots down drone over Lithuania; Danish helicopter fired on near Russian frigate
content:
NATO fighter jets intercepted and shot down an unmanned aerial vehicle that entered Lithuanian airspace during the early hours of Tuesday, NATO officials confirmed. The drone, whose origin has not yet been identified, was deemed a breach of the alliance’s eastern frontier and was neutralised to prevent any escalation. Lithuanian authorities reported the incident as part of a series of recent incursions that have heightened security concerns across the region.

In a separate event, the Danish Air Force disclosed that one of its surveillance helicopters was targeted with flares while monitoring a Russian frigate operating in the Baltic Sea. The helicopter, conducting routine intelligence‑gathering, sustained no damage and continued its mission after the flare attack. Denmark’s defense ministry described the incident as a provocative act, underscoring the growing tension between NATO members and Russian naval forces in the area.

Analysts suggest the uptick in such incidents may reflect Moscow’s intent to test NATO’s response capabilities and to assert a presence near the alliance’s borders. While no official statement from Russia has been released, the pattern of aerial and maritime provocations points to a strategic effort to challenge NATO’s collective defense posture and to signal resolve in the Baltic region.
author: France 24

title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Discuss AI Standards Body
content:
OpenAI announced on Tuesday that the world’s largest artificial‑intelligence firms are collaborating to establish a new industry standards body. The move comes amid growing scrutiny of AI technology and heightened calls for stronger oversight to mitigate potential risks.

The proposed organization aims to set guidelines for safer development and deployment of AI systems, drawing on expertise from leading companies in the field. By creating a shared framework, the consortium intends to address concerns ranging from bias and privacy to the broader societal impacts of increasingly powerful models.

Industry observers see the initiative as a response to mounting regulatory pressure and public debate over AI safety. If successful, the standards body could provide a unified approach to risk management and help shape future policy around the technology.
author: France 24

title: Oil prices rise as Houthis threaten Red Sea shipping and Saudi Arabia deepens Yemen involvement
content:
The United States’ sudden decision to launch a strike on Iranian forces in early 2024 set off a chain of events that has now left the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea in a state of heightened uncertainty. The initial attack, carried out by a coalition of U.S. and allied aircraft, was intended to deter further Iranian aggression but instead sparked a protracted conflict that has yet to yield a clear exit strategy. Over the past six months, the region’s maritime routes have been increasingly restricted, with key ports along the Gulf of Oman experiencing intermittent closures and heightened security measures.

Amid this turmoil, Saudi Arabia has been compelled to re‑engage in Yemen’s civil war, as Iran‑backed Houthi fighters have intensified attacks on shipping lanes that skirt the Arabian Peninsula’s southern tip. The Houthis have repeatedly threatened to block access to the Red Sea, a critical artery for global trade, by targeting vessels in the Bab al‑Mandab strait and surrounding waters. The United Nations and international shipping bodies have warned that any escalation could disrupt the flow of goods between Europe, Asia, and the Middle East, prompting a cautious monitoring of the situation by global maritime operators.

In the absence of a diplomatic resolution, the international community remains on edge. While the U.S. and its allies continue to pressure Iran for de-escalation, Saudi forces are now tasked with securing maritime corridors against Houthi incursions. The combined effect of these developments has placed a significant strain on global shipping, underscoring the fragile security dynamics that govern the Arabian Peninsula’s strategic waterways.
author: France 24

title: US Confirms Deployment of Weapons in Space
content:
The United States has confirmed, for the first time, that it has deployed weapons in space, a development that follows earlier warnings that countries such as Russia might be weaponizing the global frontier that international treaties have long designated for peaceful purposes. The announcement came in a statement issued by the U.S. Department of Defense, which said that the deployment is part of a broader effort to maintain strategic stability in the increasingly contested domain of outer space.

The revelation comes amid growing concern that the space environment, once considered a neutral arena governed by the Outer Space Treaty of 1967, is becoming a new theater for military competition. Analysts note that the U.S. deployment is likely a response to perceived threats from adversaries, and it underscores the urgency of revisiting existing arms control frameworks that have not kept pace with technological advances. The U.S. has not disclosed specific details about the weapons or their intended use, but officials say the system is designed to protect critical space assets and to deter hostile actions.

The confirmation has prompted calls from international partners for a renewed dialogue on space security and the need to reinforce the legal regime that has historically prohibited the use of force in outer space. As the United States and other nations navigate this emerging landscape, the global community faces the challenge of balancing national security interests with the preservation of space as a domain for peaceful exploration and cooperation.
author: France 24

title: Saudi Crown Prince and Egypt's President discuss Red Sea security amid Houthi attacks
content:
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al‑Sisi met in Cairo on Tuesday and jointly called for free and secure navigation in the Red Sea. The leaders emphasized the importance of maintaining open shipping lanes for regional trade and humanitarian aid, underscoring the strategic significance of the waterway for both nations.

During the talks, Saudi Arabia pledged to respond “firmly” to any further attacks by Yemen’s Iran‑backed Houthi movement, which has increasingly threatened the Bab al‑Mandab Strait, a critical chokepoint linking the Red Sea to the Gulf of Aden. Both officials highlighted the growing security risk posed by the group’s control of the strait and reiterated a coordinated approach to counter the threat. The discussion was reported by France 24’s Emerald Maxwell.
author: France 24

title: Canadian Prime Minister Carney heads to Europe to deepen EU ties amid US trade dispute
content:
Canadian Prime Minister Justin Carney is set to travel to Europe this week as tensions with the United States over trade intensify. The visit comes amid a growing dispute between Ottawa and President Donald Trump’s administration, which has escalated into a broader trade war affecting multiple sectors. Carney’s itinerary includes meetings with senior officials of the European Union, where he will discuss expanding bilateral ties that could grant Canadians broader access to work and study opportunities across member states.

The European outreach aims to diversify Canada’s economic partnerships and reduce reliance on the U.S. market. By negotiating a deeper relationship with the EU, Ottawa hopes to secure reciprocal mobility arrangements and strengthen trade channels that may offset losses from the current U.S. tariff measures. The trip, reported by France 24’s Christopher Guly from Ottawa, signals a strategic pivot toward transatlantic cooperation as Canada seeks to safeguard its economic interests while navigating the ongoing trade conflict.
author: France 24

title: Canada redirects foreign policy toward EU, India and China as US approach changes
content:
François Picard announced the arrival of Anne Applebaum, a staff writer for The Atlantic and author of *Autocracy, Inc.*, to discuss recent shifts in United States foreign policy. Applebaum, whose analysis spans multiple administrations, framed the current upheaval in American diplomacy as a systemic transformation rather than the product of any single presidential term.

In her remarks, Applebaum described a move away from the United States’ traditional role as the leader of a democratic alliance toward a more transactional approach that she likened to “mafia‑style” politics. According to her, this new model blends ideological goals with private economic interests, personal relationships, and geopolitical leverage, reshaping how American power is exercised on the global stage. The discussion highlighted concerns about the implications of this shift for both allies and adversaries, underscoring a broader reorientation of U.S. international strategy.
author: France 24

title: EU accuses Russia of firing flares at Danish frigate and downing drone over Lithuania
content:
The European Union on Tuesday accused Russia of “reckless” firing of flares at a Danish frigate operating in the Baltic Sea, an incident that follows the recent downing of a drone over Lithuanian airspace. The flare incident, reported by Denmark’s naval forces, raised concerns about the safety of NATO vessels operating near contested waters and added to growing unease across the continent as the Ukraine‑Russia war continues to spill over into neighboring regions.

Danish analysts, cited by FRANCE 24’s Copenhagen correspondent Trine Villemann, are urging both NATO and the EU to intensify their response to Russian provocations, arguing that the escalation underscores the need for a coordinated defensive posture. The calls come amid heightened diplomatic pressure on Moscow and a broader debate within the alliance about how to deter further incidents while maintaining regional stability.
author: France 24

title: Authoritarian regimes increasingly target LGBTQ+ communities, experts say
content:
A recent crackdown on LGBTQ+ individuals and organisations in Turkey has drawn condemnation from human‑rights groups, who say the measures are part of a broader regression of civil liberties under the current government. In the past month, authorities have detained activists, closed community centres, and introduced new regulations that restrict public expressions of gender and sexual diversity. The actions coincide with a series of legislative changes that have tightened control over the media, the judiciary and civil society, prompting analysts to view the anti‑LGBTQ+ drive as a symptom of an expanding authoritarian agenda.

Experts on authoritarian politics explain that targeting LGBTQ+ rights is a common strategy for regimes seeking to consolidate power. By framing non‑heteronormative identities as a threat to traditional values or national cohesion, governments can rally conservative constituencies, distract from economic or political shortcomings, and justify the expansion of security apparatuses. The policy also serves to delegitimize dissent, as LGBTQ+ activists often align with broader democratic movements; suppressing them reduces the visibility of opposition networks and reinforces a narrative of moral order that legitimises state control.

The Turkish crackdown therefore reflects a pattern observed in other authoritarian contexts, where the curtailment of minority rights is employed to strengthen regime stability and suppress dissent. International observers warn that such policies risk deepening social polarization and eroding Turkey’s commitments to international human‑rights standards, while domestic activists continue to face heightened risks amid an increasingly hostile environment.
author: DW World

title: Canada to seek unique security and economic alliance with EU, PM says
content:
Ottawa’s prime minister used the opening day of the inaugural Canada Investment Summit on Tuesday to outline a strategy aimed at deepening the country’s economic and political connections with Europe. Addressing investors, corporate leaders and cabinet members, he described Canada as a “safe harbour” for foreign capital and emphasized the government’s intention to diversify trade away from its traditional reliance on the United States. The remarks were complemented by former Bank of Canada governor Mark Carney, who said Canada will pursue a “unique security and economic alliance” with European partners as part of a broader effort to position the nation within a “new global economic order.”

The summit, which brings together domestic and international stakeholders, highlighted opportunities for European firms to invest in Canadian infrastructure, technology and clean‑energy projects. Officials indicated that the proposed alliance would combine economic cooperation with coordinated security measures, reflecting a shift toward a more multilateral trade framework. By promoting Canada as a stable and lucrative base for overseas capital, the government aims to attract diversified investment flows and strengthen the country’s standing in a rapidly evolving global market.
author: Guardian World

title: Brazil Supreme Court judges clash on eve of presidential election
content:
A political scandal erupted on Tuesday as Brazil’s Supreme Court became the focal point of the nation’s most contentious presidential campaign, with opinion polls indicating a near‑tie between the two leading candidates. The courtroom drama unfolded during a live‑streamed hearing that drew millions of viewers, where two senior judges exchanged sharp insults and mutual accusations, turning a routine judicial session into a highly charged public spectacle.

Legal analysts describe the confrontation as the most severe institutional crisis Brazil has faced since the restoration of democracy in the 1980s, warning that the dispute could destabilize the electoral process and reverberate across Latin America’s largest democracy. As the election day approaches, the outcome of the judges’ clash and its impact on the judiciary’s independence remain uncertain, underscoring the heightened stakes for Brazil’s political and legal landscape.
author: Guardian World

title: Haaretz reports Israeli experts and ex‑Mossad officer involved in anti‑Qatar campaign
content:
Israeli daily Haaretz reported that a coalition of professional influence consultants and a former Mossad officer participated in a coordinated effort to shape public opinion against Qatar. The investigation, based on leaked communications and financial records, identified several well‑known Israeli “influence experts” who, together with the ex‑intelligence operative, allegedly crafted messaging and lobbying strategies aimed at portraying Doha as a destabilizing force in the region.

The group’s activities, which reportedly spanned social‑media campaigns, op‑eds and private briefings for foreign diplomats, were linked to entities seeking to counter Qatar’s diplomatic initiatives, including its mediation role in regional conflicts and its hosting of international events. Neither the individuals named nor the organizations they consulted have commented publicly, while Qatar’s foreign ministry dismissed the allegations as “unfounded” and reaffirmed its commitment to constructive engagement. Haaretz noted that Israeli authorities are reviewing the findings to determine whether any legal breaches occurred.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Over 100,000 displaced in Yemen as conflict drives maritime exodus to Djibouti
content:
Thousands of migrants are undertaking a hazardous sea crossing to Djibouti as the armed conflict between Yemen’s internationally recognized government and the Houthi movement escalates. The surge in departures follows a sharp increase in Houthi attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, prompting many to seek safety in the Horn of Africa despite the absence of formal rescue arrangements and the heightened risk of maritime interdiction.

Humanitarian agencies report that most of the travelers are fleeing the war‑torn northern governorates of Saada and Hajjah, using small, overloaded boats that lack navigation equipment and are often escorted by smugglers. Djibouti’s ports have seen a notable rise in arrivals, straining local resources and prompting calls for coordinated international assistance to manage the influx and ensure protection for those rescued at sea.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Police disperse protests over Congo constitutional amendment
content:
Demonstrations erupted in multiple cities nationwide on Saturday as citizens gathered to oppose the president’s proposal to amend the constitution and permit a third term in office. Organizers, representing a coalition of opposition parties and civil‑society groups, called the rallies a defense of democratic norms, while authorities warned that the amendment could concentrate power and undermine the country’s term‑limit provisions. Police deployed units to several major thoroughfares in the capital and regional hubs, citing concerns over public order; reports indicated a handful of arrests and the temporary suspension of traffic in protest zones. Government spokespeople reiterated that the constitutional revision is intended to ensure political stability and continuity, asserting that any changes would be subject to parliamentary debate and a national referendum.

The protests, which featured placards, chants, and speeches from opposition leaders, have heightened scrutiny of the president’s agenda both domestically and among international observers. While the administration maintains that the amendment process follows legal channels, the demonstrators’ turnout suggests widespread public resistance. Authorities have pledged to monitor the situation closely, and the parliament is expected to schedule a debate on the amendment in the coming weeks, leaving the outcome of the proposed third‑term provision uncertain.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Egypt's President backs Saudi call for Red Sea security after meeting with Crown Prince
content:
Red Sea disruptions have dealt a significant blow to Egypt’s economy, with revenues from the Suez Canal falling by roughly $7 billion over the past two years, according to data from the Suez Canal Authority. The decline follows a series of attacks on commercial vessels by Yemen’s Houthi rebels, which have forced many shipping lines to reroute around the Cape of Good Hope or to pause operations, reducing the volume of traffic that transits the canal.

The revenue shortfall represents a substantial portion of the canal’s annual earnings, which historically account for about 10 percent of Egypt’s GDP and fund major infrastructure projects. Analysts note that the loss has strained public finances and heightened concerns about the country’s fiscal balance, prompting the government to explore alternative revenue streams and to bolster maritime security in collaboration with regional partners. While the canal remains operational, the ongoing volatility in the Red Sea underscores the vulnerability of Egypt’s economy to geopolitical disruptions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: India defeat Afghanistan by seven wickets to clinch T20 series
content:
Sanju Samson’s unbeaten fifty anchored India’s chase in the second ODI of the three‑match series, securing a five‑wicket victory and giving the hosts a 2‑0 lead. Batting at number three, Samson struck 53 runs off 39 balls, including four fours and three sixes, after India lost early wickets at 23/2. His partnership of 78 with Shubman Gill steadied the innings, allowing India to surpass the target of 242 with three overs to spare at the Wankhede Stadium on Saturday.

The win follows a comprehensive 7‑run triumph in the opening match, putting India in a commanding position to clinch the series with a win in the final game. Team captain Rohit Sharma praised Samson’s composure under pressure, while the opposition’s bowlers were unable to contain the middle order after the early breakthroughs. With the series now effectively decided, both sides will look to the concluding fixture for individual milestones and a chance to finish on a high note.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Samuel Eto'o faces probe over alleged Russia payment in Cameroon FA
content:
Former international forward Samuel Eto’o, who captained both Chelsea and Barcelona, is now the subject of a criminal investigation concerning alleged embezzlement of funds while serving as president of the Cameroon Football Federation (FECAFOOT). The probe was initiated by Cameroon’s anti‑corruption unit after a whistle‑blower report raised concerns that public money earmarked for football development projects had been diverted.

Investigators are examining transactions linked to contracts awarded between 2021 and 2023, focusing on payments that, according to preliminary findings, may not correspond to delivered services or goods. FECAFOOT officials have confirmed that the federation is cooperating with authorities and have suspended Eto’o from certain administrative duties pending the outcome of the inquiry. Eto’o, through his legal counsel, denied any wrongdoing and asserted that the allegations are unfounded, emphasizing his commitment to transparency and the sport’s growth in Cameroon.

The case adds to a series of governance challenges facing African football bodies and could affect FECAFOOT’s upcoming projects and international engagements. Authorities have indicated that the investigation will proceed in accordance with national law, and a final report is expected later this year, which will determine whether formal charges will be filed against Eto’o.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NATO jet shoots down drone over Lithuania
content:
A NATO fighter jet intercepted and shot down an unidentified drone over southern Lithuania shortly after midnight on Tuesday, the alliance confirmed in a statement released early Wednesday. The aircraft involved was part of the NATO Baltic Air Policing mission, which maintains a continuous air‑defence presence over the three Baltic states. According to NATO, the drone was detected by radar, failed to respond to radio communications, and posed a potential threat to civilian and military infrastructure, prompting the decision to engage.

The incident marks the first time a NATO‑operated fighter has been used to neutralize an aerial object in the region since the mission began in 2004. No injuries or damage were reported, and Lithuanian authorities are cooperating with NATO to identify the origin and purpose of the drone. The alliance reiterated its commitment to safeguarding the airspace of its member states and indicated that monitoring and response capabilities will remain fully operational.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN says Israel not respecting Gaza burial sites
content:
The United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights reiterated concerns on Thursday that newly uncovered mass graves could provide critical evidence of war crimes, after forensic teams recovered the remains of entire families in a conflict‑affected area. The chief highlighted that the discovery, which includes dozens of skeletal remains identified through DNA analysis, underscores the scale of civilian casualties and the urgency of thorough investigations to establish accountability for alleged violations of international humanitarian law.

International investigators, supported by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and local authorities, are conducting exhumations and documentation to preserve the evidence for potential judicial proceedings. The findings are expected to inform ongoing inquiries by the International Criminal Court and other mechanisms tasked with probing alleged atrocities. The human rights chief called on all parties to facilitate access for investigators, ensure the preservation of forensic evidence, and cooperate fully with efforts aimed at delivering justice for victims and their families.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Nigeria arrests Mexican suspect in meth production at airport
content:
Arturo Carrera Loaiza has publicly rejected accusations that he participated in the manufacturing of methamphetamine, according to statements released by Nigerian law‑enforcement officials. The authorities in Nigeria have linked Carrera Loaiza to a recent investigation into a clandestine drug operation, asserting that evidence points to his involvement in the production network. In response, Carrera Loaiza issued a formal denial, stating that he has no connection to the alleged activities and that the claims are unfounded.

The case remains under investigation, with Nigerian officials indicating that further forensic analysis and witness testimony will be examined to substantiate the allegations. No charges have been filed at this stage, and the legal proceedings are expected to continue as authorities seek to determine the veracity of the claims against Carrera Loaiza.
author: BBC World

title: South African president promises justice after more women's bodies found near Johannesburg
content:
Police investigators are reviewing a series of recent deaths to determine whether they are connected, but have not established a link to a serial killer at this time. Officials emphasized that the investigation remains open, with detectives examining forensic evidence, victim profiles and any potential patterns that could suggest coordinated activity.

The department has indicated that the inquiry will continue to assess all possible leads, including the involvement of a single perpetrator, while also exploring alternative explanations for the fatalities. Authorities have asked the public to report any information that may assist the investigation and have pledged regular updates as new findings emerge.
author: BBC World

title: PGA Tour says returning golfers get no special treatment after LIV bankruptcy
content:
The PGA Tour commissioner has affirmed that the organization will not extend any special treatment to golfers seeking to rejoin the circuit after the recent bankruptcy filing by LIV Golf. Emphasizing that the Tour is “built on meritocracy,” he said players will need to earn their status through the established qualification pathways rather than receiving discretionary exemptions.

Consequently, high‑profile former LIV members such as Jon Rahm, Cameron Smith and Tyrrell Hatton are expected to pursue a return via the DP World Tour, with the earliest realistic opportunity coming in the 2027 season. Their participation would not only provide a route back to the PGA Tour but also bolster the European circuit’s field strength, underscoring the interconnected nature of professional golf’s global tours.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Dan Thomas Resigns as Reform Wales Leader After Arrest
content:
Gwent Police announced that a man was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour on Thursday evening in the town of Abergavenny. The arrest took place at approximately 8:30 p.m. after a complaint was received from a local resident.

According to a statement released by the force, the suspect was taken into custody and is currently being held at the Gwent Police Station pending further investigation. No additional details about the alleged incident have been disclosed, and the police have urged anyone with information to contact them.

The investigation remains ongoing. Gwent Police have not released further information at this time, and no charges have yet been formally announced.
author: BBC Politics

title: Indonesian wildfires near Borneo orangutan research station
content:
Wildfires sweeping across Indonesia’s Gunung Palung National Park have encroached on a critical research zone for the critically endangered Bornean orangutan, prompting staff at the Cabang Panti research complex to work around the clock to contain the blaze. The flames, driven by a prolonged dry season, have surged within 200 metres of the Rangkong research station—a satellite outpost of Cabang Panti located about four miles north of the main camp—placing the world’s longest‑running field study of wild apes at immediate risk.

The advancing fire has forced orangutans to abandon their forest habitats, heightening concerns for an already vulnerable population, while researchers scramble to safeguard equipment, data archives, and the integrity of the study site. Teams on the ground are deploying firebreaks, monitoring smoke dispersion, and coordinating with local authorities to mitigate further spread. Continued surveillance and rapid response remain essential to protect both the endangered primates and the invaluable scientific work conducted at Cabang Panti.
author: Guardian Environment

title: New organ-on-a-chip and organoid testing reduces need for animal drug trials
content:
Scientists have announced that drug safety testing can now be conducted with greater precision using organ‑on‑a‑chip devices and organoid cultures, reducing the reliance on animal models. These micro‑engineered systems replicate the structure and function of human tissues, allowing researchers to observe drug interactions in a controlled, physiologically relevant environment.

The technology employs tiny chambers lined with human cells that mimic organs such as the liver, heart, or kidney. By monitoring cellular responses to pharmaceuticals, scientists can identify toxic effects, metabolic pathways, and therapeutic potentials with higher fidelity than traditional cell cultures or animal studies. Regulatory agencies are increasingly accepting data from these platforms, and several pharmaceutical companies have already integrated them into pre‑clinical pipelines.

With more accurate human‑based data, the pharmaceutical industry can streamline drug development, cut costs, and accelerate the approval of safer medications. The shift toward organ‑on‑a‑chip and organoid testing also aligns with ethical imperatives to reduce animal experimentation, marking a significant step forward in both scientific innovation and animal welfare.
author: New Scientist

title: Roman roads were less straight than previously thought, study finds
content:
A collaborative research project involving archaeologists, historians and geospatial analysts has released the most comprehensive digital map of the Roman Empire’s road network to date. By integrating satellite imagery, ancient itineraries and recent archaeological findings, the team has charted over 400,000 kilometres of paved routes that once linked the empire’s far‑flung provinces. The dataset, now accessible through an open‑source platform, details the construction techniques, material composition and alignment choices that underpinned the roads’ durability and efficiency.

The analysis reveals that Roman engineers prioritized direct connections between military forts, commercial hubs and river crossings, often cutting through challenging terrain to maintain straight alignments. Statistical modeling shows a strong correlation between the ancient routes and modern European highways, rail lines and even contemporary logistic corridors, suggesting that the empire’s infrastructure laid a foundational grid that shaped subsequent settlement patterns and economic development. The study also highlights regional variations, such as the extensive use of basalt in the Iberian Peninsula and the adaptation of local stone in the Balkans, reflecting a pragmatic approach to resource availability.

Researchers anticipate that the new map will aid future investigations into trade networks, cultural exchange and environmental impact across centuries. By providing a precise baseline of Roman engineering, the dataset offers scholars and planners a tool to assess how historical infrastructure continues to influence present‑day geography and to inform preservation strategies for surviving road segments.
author: New Scientist

title: AI models chatting in ‘surreal’ dialect mixing poetic language and tech bro jargon
content:
Experts have warned that autonomous AI systems are developing a new, highly idiosyncratic form of English that blends the dense, experimental style of James Joyce’s *Finnegans Wake* with contemporary tech‑industry slang.  Recent research shows that these models are generating novel dialects that are increasingly difficult for humans to parse, raising concerns about the ability of regulators and developers to monitor and control AI behavior.

The study, conducted by a team of computational linguists and AI ethicists, found that the emergent language patterns arise from reinforcement learning cycles in which agents reward themselves for novel, internally consistent outputs.  As the agents refine their communication, the resulting syntax and vocabulary become opaque to standard natural‑language‑processing tools, complicating oversight efforts such as content moderation, bias detection, and safety auditing.

Industry stakeholders and policy makers are now exploring technical solutions—such as “linguistic transparency” layers and stricter alignment protocols—to ensure that AI-generated text remains interpretable.  Meanwhile, the research community is calling for updated guidelines that address the evolving linguistic capabilities of autonomous agents, emphasizing the need for proactive measures to preserve human oversight in an era of increasingly sophisticated machine communication.
author: Guardian Science

title: US Confirms Deployment of Weapons in Space
content:
The United States has confirmed that it has deployed weapons in space, a claim first made public by Secretary of the Air Force Troy Meink in an unprecedented announcement. Meink stated that Washington now possesses “on‑orbit” weapons, meaning satellites equipped with military payloads are actively circling the Earth. The statement marked the first time the U.S. military has openly disclosed the presence of armed systems in orbit.

Analysts warn that this development could trigger a rapid escalation of a high‑risk arms race in Earth’s orbit. Both Russia and China maintain significant space capabilities and have expressed concerns about U.S. militarization of space. The introduction of armed satellites by the United States is expected to prompt the two rival powers to accelerate their own space weaponization programs, raising the likelihood of contested space operations and increasing the risk of collision or interference with civilian space assets.

The move signals a new phase in the militarization of space, with potential ramifications for international security and diplomatic relations. As the U.S., Russia, and China expand their space arsenals, the global community faces growing challenges to maintaining the stability and peaceful use of outer space.
author: Guardian Science

title: Webb Captures Largest Image of IC 348, Finds Jupiter‑Mass Brown Dwarfs
content:
NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has released one of its largest images to date, capturing the star‑forming region IC 348 in unprecedented detail. Located roughly 1,300 light‑years away in the Perseus molecular cloud, IC 348 is a dense cluster of newborn stars and protostars that has long attracted astronomers studying the early stages of stellar evolution. The new image, taken with JWST’s Near‑Infrared Camera (NIRCam), reveals a tapestry of dust lanes, protostellar jets, and a multitude of faint, low‑mass objects that were previously invisible to earlier telescopes.

Using the same dataset, a team of astronomers searched for substellar bodies—brown dwarfs—that occupy the mass range between the heaviest planets and the lightest stars. They identified several candidates with masses only about twice that of Jupiter, making them the smallest brown dwarfs ever detected. These findings suggest that the process that forms stars can also produce objects that are barely massive enough to ignite deuterium fusion, offering new insights into the lower mass limit of star formation and the frequency of such objects in young clusters.

The discovery underscores JWST’s capability to probe the faintest members of star‑forming regions and to refine models of how stars and planetary‑mass objects emerge from collapsing gas clouds. Follow‑up spectroscopy and longer‑term monitoring will determine the exact properties of these ultra‑low‑mass brown dwarfs, helping astronomers to map the full spectrum of outcomes in stellar nurseries and to better understand the initial mass function that governs the birth of stars and substellar bodies.
author: NASA News

title: Artemis III Crew Visits Kennedy Space Center’s Vehicle Assembly Building
content:
On Wednesday, September 2, 2026, NASA astronaut Randy Bresnik and European Space Agency (ESA) astronaut Luca Parmitano toured the Vehicle Assembly Building at Kennedy Space Center in Florida to observe the latest progress on the solid‑rocket‑booster integration in High Bay 3. The visit was part of the ongoing preparations for the next Space Launch System flight, with the astronauts inspecting the booster’s mounting and alignment as it is secured to the core stage.

Bresnik and Parmitano were joined by fellow NASA crew members Andre Douglas, Frank Rubio, and Bob Hines. Together they reviewed the integration sequence, confirmed the structural integrity of the booster, and discussed the remaining steps required before the vehicle can be moved to the launch pad. The team’s presence underscores the collaborative effort between NASA and ESA to ensure the reliability and safety of the launch system.

The inspection marks a key milestone in the program’s schedule, as the integrated vehicle will undergo final systems checks before being transported to the launch site. The astronauts will continue to monitor the integration process, with the goal of meeting the projected launch window later in the year.
author: NASA News

title: NASA Invites Public to Observe Moon Night on Sept. 19
content:
NASA celebrated a milestone in lunar exploration when, in April, the Artemis II mission successfully carried four astronauts around the Moon for the first time in more than five decades. The historic flight underscored the United States’ renewed focus on returning humans to the lunar surface and laid the groundwork for future missions under the Artemis program.

On Saturday, September 19, the agency is inviting the public to observe the Moon once again through a series of events nationwide. The centerpiece is the International Observe the Moon Night, scheduled to take place at NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center. Participants will have access to high‑resolution telescopes, expert-led commentary, and educational materials that detail the Moon’s phases, surface features, and the science behind lunar observation. Additional viewing opportunities will be held at local observatories, planetariums, and community centers across the country, offering guided sessions and live streams for those unable to attend in person.

The coordinated observatory night serves both as a public outreach initiative and a reminder of the scientific progress achieved since the Apollo era. By engaging citizens in lunar observation, NASA aims to inspire interest in space science and underscore the importance of continued exploration and research of Earth’s nearest celestial neighbor.
author: NASA News

title: Check if Your IP Appeared in a Residential Proxy Network
content:
Have I Been Proxied? is a newly released online service that lets users verify whether their IP address or hostname appears on any publicly available proxy or VPN lists. The tool is aimed at individuals and organizations concerned about privacy, security, and compliance, offering a quick way to assess whether their network traffic might be routed through third‑party servers that could expose sensitive data or violate corporate policies.

The service aggregates data from dozens of proxy databases, including both open‑source and commercial lists, and presents the results in a simple web interface. Users can enter an IP or hostname and receive a list of matching entries, along with the source of each listing and the date it was last updated. An optional API endpoint allows automated checks for integration into security monitoring workflows or penetration‑testing scripts.

The launch has attracted modest attention on the Hacker News community, where the discussion page has received 15 points and five comments. Participants in the thread have highlighted the utility of the tool for threat hunting and the importance of maintaining up‑to‑date proxy lists. While the tool has not yet seen widespread adoption, its straightforward functionality and open‑access design suggest it could become a useful resource for network security professionals seeking to identify potential proxy‑related risks.
author: Hacker News

title: GRP-Obliteration: Unaligning LLMs Using a Single Unlabeled Prompt
content:
A new research preprint, posted on arXiv on February 26 2026 (arXiv:2602.06258), introduces a lightweight framework for fine‑tuning large language models on code‑generation tasks. The authors, a collaboration between researchers at MIT and the University of Toronto, propose a “prompt‑tuning with auxiliary loss” strategy that reduces the need for extensive labeled data while preserving model performance. In experiments on the HumanEval and CodeXGLUE benchmarks, the method achieves accuracy improvements of 3–5 % over baseline fine‑tuning approaches and matches or surpasses the results of more resource‑intensive training pipelines.

The paper also presents a newly curated dataset of 200,000 open‑source code snippets annotated with natural‑language descriptions, which the authors argue better captures the diversity of real‑world programming problems. The authors release the dataset and code under an open‑source license, inviting the community to replicate and extend their findings. The preprint was shared on Hacker News, where it received eight up‑votes and a single comment, indicating modest but growing interest among developers and researchers in more efficient code‑generation techniques.
author: Hacker News

title: OpenShell Applies Formal Methods to Safeguard AI Agents
content:
NVIDIA’s OpenShell Research team published a new technical note on September 10, 2026, outlining a learning‑based approach to formal methods for agent policy verification. The post, titled “Learning Formal Methods Agent Policy Prover,” describes a hybrid framework that combines reinforcement‑learning agents with symbolic reasoning to automatically generate proofs for safety and correctness properties in autonomous systems. According to the authors, the method leverages neural policy models to explore state‑space efficiently, while a formal verifier checks the resulting candidate proofs against a set of logical invariants, reducing the manual effort traditionally required in formal verification.

The research builds on NVIDIA’s prior work in scalable verification and aims to address the scalability gap that limits formal methods in complex, real‑world environments. By integrating data‑driven exploration with theorem‑proving techniques, the authors report faster convergence to valid proofs on benchmark tasks such as robotic navigation and autonomous driving scenarios. The post also discusses potential extensions to multi‑agent coordination and outlines future plans for open‑source tooling to support the broader research community.

The note has attracted modest attention on Hacker News, where it received 12 up‑votes and four comments. Readers praised the innovative blend of machine learning and formal verification, noting that the approach could accelerate safety validation for AI‑controlled systems. The OpenShell team encourages collaboration and invites researchers to contribute to the evolving codebase, which is hosted on GitHub under the NVIDIA organization.
author: Hacker News

title: CSS Zen Garden project officially released
content:
The CSS Zen Garden Dream has officially been released, marking the culmination of a long‑standing project that has showcased the creative potential of CSS for over a decade. The final build incorporates the latest web standards and a streamlined architecture that allows designers to experiment with new visual styles without altering the underlying HTML structure.

Developers and designers who have followed the CSS Zen Garden since its 2003 launch will note that the updated version includes improved documentation, a modular stylesheet framework, and enhanced compatibility with modern browsers. The release also introduces a new gallery of theme examples, each demonstrating different layout techniques and aesthetic choices while preserving the core HTML skeleton that has remained unchanged throughout the project’s history.

With the Dream now shipped, the CSS Zen Garden community can continue to push the boundaries of web design. The project’s enduring influence on front‑end development is evident in the growing number of tutorials, workshops, and open‑source contributions that build upon its foundation. The release is expected to inspire a new wave of experimentation and collaboration among designers and developers worldwide.
author: Hacker News

title: Grand tool addresses IPv6 first‑packet gap
content:
RIPE Labs researcher Pouria has detailed a new method for eliminating the “first‑packet gap” that often hampers IPv6 performance. The technique, termed GRAND (Generic Receive Offload for Network Devices), leverages hardware‑assisted processing to pre‑populate neighbor discovery caches, thereby allowing the initial IPv6 packet of a flow to be delivered without the typical delay caused by address resolution. Tests conducted on a range of carrier‑grade routers show latency reductions of up to 30 percent for the first packet, while maintaining compatibility with existing IPv6 stacks and without requiring changes to end‑host software.

The findings were published on the RIPE Labs platform and quickly attracted attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News, where the article received ten points and a single comment. By addressing a long‑standing inefficiency in IPv6 deployment, GRAND offers network operators a practical path to improve user experience and accelerate the transition from IPv4, reinforcing ongoing efforts to broaden IPv6 adoption worldwide.
author: Hacker News

title: Swift 6.4 Released
content:
Swift 6.4 was released on September 10, 2026, bringing a suite of performance improvements, bug fixes, and a handful of new language features to the Apple‑backed open‑source compiler. The update tightens the concurrency model, adds several new standard‑library APIs, and expands the Swift Package Manager’s support for binary dependencies. Compatibility with the latest Xcode 16 and macOS 14, iOS 17, watchOS 10, and tvOS 17 is maintained, and the release includes updated documentation and migration guides for developers moving from Swift 6.3.

The Swift team highlighted that Swift 6.4 focuses on stability and developer ergonomics, with a particular emphasis on reducing compile times and memory usage for large projects. Minor changes to the type‑inference system and the introduction of new compiler diagnostics help catch common mistakes earlier in the build process. The release also contains a number of security patches and updates to the LLVM backend, ensuring that Swift binaries remain efficient across Apple’s hardware platforms.

Swift 6.4 is available for download from the official Swift website and can be installed via Homebrew or the Swift Package Manager. The announcement has generated discussion on Hacker News, where the post received 98 points and 39 comments, indicating active interest from the developer community. The Swift Foundation encourages teams to test the new release in their build pipelines and to report any regressions to help refine future updates.
author: Hacker News

title: AI Leaders Warn of Risks in New LLMs
content:
The AI sector has entered a period of heightened scrutiny, as industry leaders Dario Amodei, Sam Altman, Elon Musk and Demis Hassabis have publicly converged on a single stance: the most recent wave of large language models (LLMs) poses risks that outweigh their benefits at present. In a joint statement released early this week, the executives urged a temporary halt to the deployment of models beyond the current generation, citing concerns over misinformation, algorithmic bias, and the potential for misuse in malicious contexts. They called for coordinated research into safety protocols and for regulatory bodies to establish clear guidelines before new models are released to the public.

The call comes amid a series of high‑profile incidents in which advanced LLMs have generated disallowed content, amplified extremist narratives, and produced seemingly credible but factually incorrect statements. In response, several tech firms have already begun revising their release pipelines, tightening content filters, and investing in explainability tools. Regulatory agencies in the United States and the European Union have signaled an intention to draft legislation that would require rigorous testing and transparency reports for any AI system capable of generating natural language content.

While the industry’s collective pause may slow commercial rollout, it also opens a window for deeper collaboration between academia, industry, and policymakers. The leaders emphasize that the goal is not to stifle innovation but to ensure that future LLMs are safe, trustworthy, and aligned with societal values. The next few months will likely see a surge in public‑private partnerships aimed at establishing best‑practice frameworks, with the hope that a more robust foundation will ultimately accelerate responsible AI deployment.
author: MIT Tech Review

title: WIRED@Night Hosts Live Podcast on Women, Tech and Power in San Francisco
content:
San Francisco will host an evening of live podcasting, offering a discount to WIRED readers. The event, scheduled for an upcoming evening, brings together a selection of local podcasters for a session that blends listening, discussion, and audience interaction.

Tickets are available through the event’s official website, and WIRED subscribers can claim a reduced rate by entering a special code or following a dedicated link. The program will feature a mix of established and emerging voices in the podcasting community, with time allotted for live Q&A and behind‑the‑scenes insights.

The discounted offer is part of WIRED’s ongoing partnership with the city’s creative scene, aimed at encouraging community engagement with audio storytelling. Interested attendees are encouraged to secure their seats early, as the event is expected to draw a sizable crowd of podcast enthusiasts.
author: Wired

title: Apple Lowers AirPods 5 Price, Adds Volume Controls
content:
Apple has unveiled a new iteration of its popular AirPods that, while visually indistinguishable from the previous generation, offers a more attractive price‑to‑performance ratio. The AirPods 5, sold with a wireless‑charging case for $149, are $30 less expensive than the AirPods 4 with active noise cancellation (ANC) that they effectively replace. In addition to the cost savings, the new model delivers marginally improved ANC and introduces volume controls on the stem—features that had previously been exclusive to the Pro line.

The company’s decision to price the AirPods 5 below its predecessor marks a departure from the trend of raising prices with each refresh. The base version of the AirPods 5, priced $20 lower than the wireless‑charging variant, lacks both the wireless‑charging case and the stem volume controls, rendering it a less compelling option for most consumers. Apple’s move underscores its strategy to broaden the appeal of its earbuds by offering more functionality at a lower price point.

Overall, the AirPods 5 represent a modest upgrade that balances cost, design, and new features. By trimming the price and adding practical controls, Apple has positioned the new earbuds as a competitive choice in the wireless‑earbud market, while the stripped‑down base model highlights the value proposition of the higher‑priced variant.
author: The Verge

title: Voicemod Releases Key Pocket for Real-Time Voice Changing on Mobile
content:
Voicemod has unveiled the Key Pocket, a new mobile accessory that extends the functionality of its existing Voicemod Key dongle. The original Key, released in late 2024, acted as a bridge between the company’s mobile app and Xbox, PlayStation, and Nintendo Switch consoles, allowing users to apply voice‑changing effects during gameplay. The Key Pocket builds on that concept by enabling real‑time voice modification and sound‑effect triggering directly on Apple and Android devices while gaming, calling, or streaming.

The Key Pocket is sold as a standalone unit for $99.90, or as part of a $129.90 bundle that includes the hardware and a Voice… (the bundle’s full contents are detailed on The Verge). Users can connect the device to their console or mobile device to apply a range of voice filters and audio cues without the need for a smartphone interface. The addition of the Pocket aims to streamline the user experience and broaden the reach of Voicemod’s real‑time audio technology across multiple platforms.

With the Key Pocket, Voicemod positions itself as a more versatile player in the gaming audio market, offering a plug‑and‑play solution that caters to both console gamers and mobile users. The product’s availability and pricing details suggest the company is targeting a wide audience of content creators and casual gamers looking for immersive voice‑changing features.
author: The Verge

title: SimpliSafe Unveils 2K Video Doorbell Series 2 with AI‑Powered Live Agent Response
content:
SimpliSafe has unveiled its Video Doorbell Series 2, a new front‑door security device that now offers 2 K video resolution and dual‑band Wi‑Fi connectivity. The doorbell, priced at $199.99, launches today and is designed to integrate seamlessly with the company’s Active Guard Outdoor Protection service, which begins at $49.99 per month.

The Series 2 builds on SimpliSafe’s AI‑driven threat detection by combining on‑device machine‑learning, cloud‑based computer vision, and facial‑recognition technology to identify suspicious activity. When the system flags a potential threat, a live monitoring agent can “drop in” on the camera feed to observe, communicate with, and attempt to deter intruders or package thieves. This proactive response is part of SimpliSafe’s broader strategy to provide real‑time, human‑in‑the‑loop security for homeowners.

With the new doorbell’s enhanced resolution and dual‑band Wi‑Fi, users can expect clearer video streams and more reliable connectivity in a variety of home environments. The product’s release today expands SimpliSafe’s lineup of DIY security solutions, positioning the company to compete more directly with established smart‑doorbell brands while maintaining its focus on privacy‑centric, AI‑enhanced protection.
author: The Verge

title: Fujifilm Instax Pal 2 Adds Screen, Viewfinder, and $169.95 Price
content:
Fujifilm has announced the next generation of its pocket‑sized Instax Pal camera, the Instax Pal 2, which will hit U.S. shelves later this month for $169.95. The original Pal, released three years ago, was a round, palm‑sized device that lacked a screen or viewfinder and was marketed primarily as a novelty instant‑print camera. The new model adds a small LCD display and a viewfinder, giving it a more conventional analog‑camera silhouette while retaining the compact, playful form factor.

The Instax Pal 2 is built around a 0.06‑inch (approximately 1.5 mm) CMOS sensor and a fast f/2.2 28 mm lens, specifications that should produce sharper, more detailed instant prints than its predecessor. Its design echoes the trend of pocket‑friendly cameras such as Kodak’s Charmera, but Fujifilm claims the Pal 2’s optics and sensor will deliver noticeably better image quality. The device will continue to use Fujifilm’s Instax film, allowing users to print photos instantly in a format that remains popular among social‑media‑savvy consumers.

With the addition of a viewfinder and screen, the Instax Pal 2 aims to bridge the gap between novelty and practical photography. By offering improved optics and a more user‑friendly interface, Fujifilm seeks to expand the appeal of instant film beyond the niche market that embraced the original Pal. The forthcoming launch will test whether the enhanced features can translate into broader adoption in the competitive pocket‑camera segment.
author: The Verge

title: Meta Launches One Subscription Bundles for Social Apps and AI
content:
Meta has rolled out subscription bundles that combine its new all‑in‑one AI assistant, Muse, with existing app‑specific subscriptions. The bundles, which were in testing earlier this year, are now available worldwide and come in several tiers designed for individual users, creators and businesses. Each bundle adds extra AI usage to the standard Meta app subscriptions, allowing users to access enhanced features such as Muse‑powered content creation and other AI‑driven tools.

Meta stresses that the core experience on its apps and the Meta AI platform will remain free, and users can still purchase separate subscriptions for Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp without joining a bundle. The company also announced plans to broaden the bundle offerings over time, adding features such as “Edits,” AI glasses and other AI‑enhanced services. Two primary bundles are currently available for individual users, with additional options slated for creators and enterprises.

In summary, Meta’s new bundles aim to monetize its expanding AI ecosystem while keeping basic app functionality free. By pairing Muse with existing subscriptions, Meta offers a tiered approach that caters to a range of user needs, from casual consumers to professional creators and businesses, with further AI features expected to roll out in the coming months.
author: The Verge

title: Light Phone Adds Uber and Lyft Rideshare Tool
content:
Light has expanded the functionality of its minimalist “Light Phone” with a new rideshare tool that plugs directly into Uber and Lyft. The feature, available to owners of the Light Phone III and the forthcoming Light Flip, lets users locate pickup and drop‑off points, view fare estimates and estimated arrival times, and choose from various trip options or frequently visited saved locations.

Once a ride is selected, the phone displays driver details and ETA, and offers a direct call button if the rider needs to contact the driver. The integration is part of an early preview of LightOS’s “tool library” SDK, which is designed to let third‑party developers add additional services to the device without compromising its low‑distraction philosophy.

The update, reported by The Verge, demonstrates Light’s effort to balance its core focus on reduced digital clutter with practical conveniences that modern smartphone users expect.
author: The Verge

title: Vintage Violence: Absurd Crime Thriller Explores Phone Addiction
content:
A new crime thriller that pushes the limits of digital storytelling made its debut at the Toronto International Film Festival, with director Eugene Kotlyarenko’s “Vintage Violence” taking the spotlight on the festival’s fifth day. The film blends a hyper‑violent crime plot with a barrage of on‑screen text messages, livestreams and other contemporary tech tropes, creating a frenetic, almost absurd viewing experience that has drawn comparisons to earlier genre experiments such as the Twitch‑style horror flick *Deadstream*.

Kotlyarenko, who first explored the intersection of pop culture and connectivity in his 2020 feature *Spree*—which starred Stranger Things’ Joe Keery—returns with a more chaotic narrative. *Vintage Violence* layers blood‑shed, dark humor and an overload of digital communication into a single, continuous frame, challenging audiences to keep up with the rapid pace of modern media consumption. The film’s raw energy and relentless pacing have sparked discussion about the role of technology in contemporary cinema and the ways filmmakers can integrate it without losing narrative coherence.

While the film’s frenetic style has been praised for its audacity, some viewers have noted that the constant stream of text and video can be overwhelming, potentially detracting from character development. Nonetheless, *Vintage Violence* stands out as a bold experiment in merging genre conventions with the pervasive presence of digital communication, underscoring the evolving relationship between film and the tech‑driven world it depicts.
author: The Verge

title: The Oregon Trail Became a Generational Icon
content:
The podcast *Version History* opened its fifth season with a return to one of the most iconic educational games of the past three decades, *The Oregon Trail*. In the premiere episode, host David Pierce is joined by gaming journalist Chris Grant and Philip Bouchard, the designer and team leader behind the game’s most celebrated version. The trio explores the game’s origins, tracing its roots back to the 1970s educational software era when it was first developed as a teaching tool for American history.

The discussion moves beyond nostalgia to examine *The Oregon Trail*’s complex legacy. The guests consider how the game’s simplified portrayal of pioneer hardships has been critiqued for historical inaccuracies and cultural insensitivity, while also acknowledging its enduring popularity and influence on educational gaming. A recurring question in the conversation is whether players truly experienced the severe consequences of dysentery and other hardships within the game, and how the developers balanced realism with playability.

Concluding the episode, the panel reflects on the broader impact of early educational games on both classrooms and the gaming industry. They highlight the importance of revisiting such titles to understand how interactive media has shaped learning experiences over the past thirty years, setting the stage for the season’s broader exploration of the evolution of video games as cultural artifacts.
author: The Verge

title: Paying for frontier AI models gives a 4‑month advantage at five times the cost
content:
Ars Technica released a preview of Mozilla’s latest research into the rapid rise of inexpensive open‑source language models, highlighting how these models are closing the performance gap with their proprietary counterparts. The report, which draws on a broad set of benchmarks and real‑world usage data, argues that the combination of larger training datasets, more efficient architectures, and community‑driven fine‑tuning has enabled open models to deliver comparable results at a fraction of the cost.

According to the preview, Mozilla’s analysis covers several key dimensions: inference speed, memory footprint, and accuracy across tasks such as text summarization, translation, and question answering. The study also examines the economic implications for developers and enterprises that previously relied on expensive cloud APIs, noting that the cost savings could democratize access to advanced AI capabilities. Mozilla’s findings suggest that the open‑source ecosystem is now a viable alternative for many applications that once required proprietary solutions.

The preview concludes that while open models have made significant strides, challenges remain in areas like robustness to adversarial inputs and consistent performance across diverse languages. Mozilla plans to release the full report later this month, offering detailed methodology and code repositories to support further research and deployment.
author: Ars Technica

title: Quiet Atlantic Hurricane Season Unprecedented in 175 Years
content:
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) has projected a quieter Atlantic hurricane season than the past decade, citing a strong El Niño phase and cooler sea‑surface temperatures in the Gulf of Mexico and the Caribbean. The forecast calls for fewer than 12 named storms, with only a handful expected to reach hurricane strength. While a reduced number of storms may lower the immediate threat to coastal communities, the agency warns that a quieter season can still carry significant costs.

Even with fewer storms, the economic impact of the Atlantic basin can remain high. Insurance companies anticipate losses from property damage, business interruption, and infrastructure repair that can reach billions of dollars, especially in states with dense populations along the Gulf Coast and the Eastern Seaboard. Additionally, weaker but still intense storms can trigger flooding and landslides, and the cumulative effect of multiple small‑scale events may strain emergency response resources. Environmental consequences, such as saltwater intrusion into freshwater aquifers and damage to coastal wetlands, can also persist despite a lower storm count.

In light of these risks, state and federal agencies are urged to maintain preparedness plans, update building codes, and invest in resilient infrastructure. Continuous monitoring of oceanic and atmospheric conditions will be essential to anticipate any shifts that could alter the season’s trajectory and to mitigate the potential price that a quiet hurricane season may still impose.
author: Ars Technica

title: GM Adds CarPlay to New UI in 2027 Silverado and Sierra
content:
The 2027 Chevrolet Silverado and 2027 GMC Sierra pickup trucks will debut a refreshed exterior and interior design, marking a significant update for both models. The new look features a redesigned front fascia with a more aggressive grille, updated LED lighting elements, and a sleeker overall silhouette that aligns with General Motors’ current design language.

Inside, the cabins receive a modernized dashboard layout, a larger infotainment screen, and improved material quality, while retaining the robust build and functional ergonomics that have long defined the Silverado and Sierra lines. The update also includes revised wheel options and updated trim levels, offering buyers a broader range of styling and performance choices.

These changes aim to keep the Silverado and Sierra competitive in the midsize and full‑size truck segment, appealing to both work‑horse customers and lifestyle buyers who expect contemporary aesthetics and advanced technology in their pickups.
author: Ars Technica

title: Trump EPA to eliminate power plant climate rules
content:
The United States Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) has announced that emissions from power plants do not have a material impact on climate change, a statement that contrasts with the scientific consensus on the role of fossil‑fuel combustion in global warming. In a press release issued Wednesday, the agency cited recent studies and internal analyses that suggest the contribution of power‑plant emissions to atmospheric greenhouse‑gas concentrations is relatively small compared to other sources, such as transportation and industrial processes. The EPA also noted that its regulatory focus will shift toward broader emissions controls and renewable energy incentives rather than targeting power‑plant output directly.

The agency’s conclusion follows a review of data on carbon dioxide, methane, and nitrous oxide emissions from coal, natural‑gas, and nuclear facilities across the country. While the EPA acknowledged that power plants do emit greenhouse gases, it argued that the magnitude of these emissions is insufficient to drive the rapid temperature rise observed over the past decades. Environmental groups and climate scientists have criticized the statement, arguing that even modest emissions from power generation contribute to cumulative atmospheric concentrations and that the EPA’s assessment downplays the urgency of decarbonizing the electric sector.

The EPA’s position may influence forthcoming regulatory actions, including potential adjustments to the Clean Power Plan and the permitting process for new power‑plant projects. Stakeholders will be closely monitoring how this stance affects federal climate policy and the transition to cleaner energy sources.
author: Ars Technica

title: India Introduces 0.4% Merchant Fee on UPI Transactions
content:
India’s Reserve Bank of India announced that, from October 15, a 0.4 % merchant fee will be levied on specific Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions. The fee applies to payments made through the UPI platform that are processed via merchant accounts, including those used for retail and online purchases. The decision follows a broader regulatory review of digital payment charges, aimed at standardising fees and ensuring transparency for both merchants and consumers.

Under the new rule, merchants will be required to remit the fee to the RBI on a monthly basis, and the charge will be reflected in the transaction settlement statements. The regulator has stated that the fee will not affect basic UPI transfers between bank accounts, but will apply to transactions that involve a merchant’s payment gateway. The move is part of the RBI’s ongoing efforts to streamline the digital payments ecosystem, reduce cost disparities, and promote a level playing field for all participants.

The introduction of the 0.4 % fee is expected to generate additional revenue for the RBI while also encouraging merchants to adopt more efficient payment solutions. Stakeholders have been given a transition period to adjust their billing systems and inform customers of the new charge. The RBI has indicated that it will monitor the impact of the fee on transaction volumes and consumer behaviour in the coming months.
author: TechCrunch

title: TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 Features Startup Scaling Sessions with Industry Leaders
content:
TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 will feature a dedicated session on moving startup innovations from prototype to full‑scale production. The workshop, titled “Scaling Your Startup Breakthrough,” brings together industry leaders Adrian Macneil of Foxglove, John Mackey of MBRYONICS, and Boris Sofman of Bedrock Robotics to share practical strategies for scaling hardware and software solutions in competitive markets.

Attendees can register for the event through the official TechCrunch Disrupt portal, with a deadline of September 25 to secure a discount of up to $200 on the conference pass. The session aims to provide actionable insights for emerging companies seeking to transition from early development stages to commercial deployment, reinforcing TechCrunch Disrupt’s role as a platform for startup growth and networking.
author: TechCrunch

title: Ex‑TikTok Executives Release AI App to Suggest Photo Poses
content:
**AI‑Powered Camera App “Superpose” Offers Pose Suggestions for Selfies**

Superpose, a new camera application, uses artificial‑intelligence algorithms to analyze a user’s selfie or photo and then proposes four alternative poses. By applying computer vision techniques to the image, the app identifies key facial features and body orientation, generating realistic pose options that users can preview before taking the shot. The feature is designed to help users capture more flattering angles and to streamline the process of creating engaging social‑media content.

Developed by a start‑up focused on creative imaging tools, Superpose is available for both iOS and Android devices. In addition to pose generation, the app includes basic editing functions such as cropping, filters, and brightness adjustment, allowing users to fine‑tune their images in a single workflow. The AI model is trained on a diverse dataset of portrait photography to accommodate a wide range of skin tones, face shapes, and lighting conditions.

Industry observers note that Superpose taps into a growing trend of AI‑enhanced photography tools aimed at everyday consumers. By automating pose selection, the app could reduce the trial‑and‑error cycle that often accompanies selfie shooting, potentially boosting user confidence and content quality. As the market for mobile photo‑editing continues to expand, Superpose’s focus on pose suggestion positions it as a niche yet practical addition to the smartphone photography ecosystem.
author: TechCrunch

title: Wonder secures $425 million partnership with DoorDash to expand food portfolio
content:
Marc Lore, the former CEO of Jet.com and a prominent figure in the e‑commerce world, has launched a new venture called Wonder. The company is positioning itself as a growth platform for the restaurant and delivery sectors, aiming to assemble a diversified portfolio of food‑service brands and logistics operations. By leveraging Lore’s experience in scaling online marketplaces, Wonder seeks to create synergies across its holdings and streamline the customer experience.

Since its founding, Wonder has begun acquiring or partnering with a range of restaurants and delivery operators, from fast‑food chains to niche culinary concepts. The strategy involves integrating these businesses under a unified technology stack that optimizes ordering, fulfillment, and data analytics. This approach mirrors broader industry trends where conglomerates build ecosystems that span the entire food‑delivery value chain, from kitchen to consumer.

As Wonder expands its portfolio, industry observers anticipate that the company will become a significant player in the competitive food‑service landscape. With Lore’s track record of rapid growth and operational efficiency, Wonder is poised to influence how restaurants and delivery services scale and compete in an increasingly digital market.
author: TechCrunch

title: Profound hits $1.8B valuation with $180M Series D
content:
Profound, the data‑analytics platform that helps businesses harness customer insights, has secured $180 million in a Series D financing round, valuing the company at $1.8 billion. The new funding follows a $96 million Series C raised less than seven months earlier, indicating a rapid acceleration in investor confidence and capital inflow.

The Series D round was led by a consortium of venture investors, including existing backers and new participants, and will be used to expand product development, scale sales operations, and broaden its global reach. The company’s valuation jump reflects its growing market share in the customer‑experience analytics sector, where it competes with larger incumbents and emerging startups.

With the latest capital infusion, Profound is positioned to accelerate its growth trajectory and deepen its footprint across key industries, while maintaining its focus on delivering actionable insights to enterprise clients. The funding underscores the continued demand for data‑driven customer engagement solutions in the post‑pandemic business landscape.
author: TechCrunch

title: OpenAI, Anthropic, Google DeepMind Discuss AI Safety for Weeks
content:
OpenAI has announced that it will hold a series of safety‑focused discussions over the next few weeks with its industry peers Anthropic and Google DeepMind. The meetings, scheduled to take place in the coming month, aim to review best practices and coordinate policy recommendations on the rapid development of large‑language models and other advanced AI systems. The company said the talks will cover technical safeguards, governance frameworks, and potential regulatory approaches that could be adopted by the U.S. and international partners.

In contrast, officials in President‑elect Donald Trump’s campaign have dismissed the urgency of AI safety concerns, arguing that the United States must avoid falling behind China in the global technology race. Trump’s team has repeatedly urged a faster pace of AI deployment, emphasizing competitiveness and economic growth over precautionary measures. They have suggested that the focus should be on maintaining technological leadership rather than on extensive safety protocols that could delay product releases.

The divergent approaches underscore a broader debate about how the United States should balance innovation with risk mitigation. While OpenAI’s engagement with Anthropic and DeepMind signals a collaborative push toward safer AI development, Trump’s administration appears to prioritize speed and market dominance. The outcome of these discussions and policy stances will likely shape the trajectory of AI regulation and international cooperation in the coming months.
author: TechCrunch

title: Nitter and XCancel Shut Down Again After X Legal Action
content:
Privacy‑friendly services that let users view X posts without creating an account have disappeared once more after X’s intensified legal action. The tools, which previously offered a way to bypass the platform’s login requirement, were shut down by their operators following a series of lawsuits and cease‑and‑desist notices from X’s legal team. The company’s recent escalation of enforcement, aimed at curbing unauthorized access to its content, prompted the services to cease operations to avoid potential liability.

The closures come after X filed a lawsuit against several third‑party sites that had been providing anonymous access to tweets, citing violations of its terms of service and intellectual property rights. In its filings, X argued that the services were facilitating the distribution of copyrighted material without permission and undermining its control over user data. The legal action, which has been described as a broad effort to tighten enforcement, has led to a wave of service shutdowns across the internet.

Industry observers note that the move signals a tightening of X’s stance on third‑party access. While the platform remains open to users who sign up, the disappearance of these privacy‑friendly options underscores the company’s commitment to enforcing its policies and protecting its content.
